reviewer: Kimi main recovery executor actually viewed the exact source and NEAREST 8x detail including the note crop, complete unchanged current raw, full white/cyan/source-alpha/return-alpha sheet and unchanged naiwa reference; compared note grouping, cap, brows, pose, collar, tab and backing, with generation and evidence bindings checked by the review recorder.

remaining_reasons: The exact source has TWO separated irregular gray-mark groups in its upper note row and TWO in its lower row. External-04 expands these into many separate round dots and short blobs, including an extra lower stroke under the upper-left group. Restore only the two source-scale irregular groups in EACH row with their original relative lengths, spacing and compact footprint, not a multiplied generic dot/dash pattern or readable writing.

hair_features.reason: The dark brows remain beneath the cap visor; cap-covered hair and clean upper-lip/chin treatment are retained without an invented beard or glasses.

collar_fit.reason: The navy standing collar fits the rounded chin and short broad neck transition without pinching, floating cloth or a cream bib.

entries.positive_observation: The white/light-gray topped navy cap, gold badge and visor, dark brows, green-ringed black eyes, one mouth, dark navy collar detail and leftward pose remain. The complete frame/backplate and small right-edge note tab remain; white/cyan/alpha viewing shows genuine exterior transparency with no visible interior holes.
entries.alpha_decision: The native exterior is acceptable on white/cyan/alpha inspection and near-opacity is not a rejection ground. The note's visible RGB grouping and multiplied dots remain incompatible with the exact source, so this is rejected for art repair rather than approved for production.
entries.visible_limitations: Cap shadow and 65x67 source resolution limit the finest upper-lip and badge detail; note glyph identities are not guessed. Rejection is for clearly changed gray-mark grouping, not unreadable lettering.
